assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins established, with ruthenium-modified proteins and kinetic measurements, that tunnelling rates follow distance and the intervening medium. This gives the physical framework (Marcus-type rates, tunnelling pathways, hopping) for respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer, the kind of mechanism stated in physical terms that I value.
assessment.attribution: Two credited names, a natural pairing with a clear shared line of work; the broader field (Marcus, Moser and Dutton, Beratan and Onuchic, Hopfield) is partly already recognised or adjacent, so the exact scope of the claim needs careful definition.
assessment.maturity: Mature, over four decades, with extensive independent confirmation and textbook status; recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority relative to Dutton, Moser, Beratan and others outside the credited names.
Marcus's 1992 prize covers the theory, so the committee must frame the experimental contribution as distinct.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic-level structure of the nitrogenase MoFe-protein and FeMo-cofactor, the central carbide and the E4 hydride intermediate, plus mechanistic work on N2 reduction, address one of biology's most important and difficult catalytic reactions. Strong biochemical and biophysical mechanism content.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the structural work, Einsle the interstitial carbide and later structures, Seefeldt the kinetic mechanism and hydride intermediates. Dean, Ribbe and others have strong claims, so the three-person limit forces a contestable choice.
assessment.maturity: Structure is confirmed independently; the full catalytic mechanism and the exact binding of N2 remain debated, so part of the story is still open.
uncertainties: Whether the mechanism is settled enough, versus a structure-only prize.
Allocation of credit among Dean, Ribbe, Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a concept at the core of respiratory enzymes, photosystem II and molecular electrocatalysis. Combined experimental thermochemistry, kinetics and theory give a general physical language for concerted proton-electron movement. This is close to my own field, so I will scrutinise it for rigour.
assessment.attribution: Mayer for bond-strength and concerted PCET framework, Nocera for model systems and artificial photosynthesis, Hammes-Schiffer for the theory; Meyer is an early pioneer. Credit is spread over a line of work rather than one discovery.
assessment.maturity: Concept widely accepted and used; the theory is still developing for complex enzyme cases.
uncertainties: Whether it is a clearly attributable discovery or a broad line of work.
Priority of Meyer and others, and the limit of three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes small-molecule pharmacology by hijacking E3 ligases to remove proteins, with PROTACs now in clinical trials, and molecular glues linked to thalidomide's mechanism. Substantial chemical-biology impact with new chemical mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies for the original PROTAC concept, Ciulli for structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex design. Handa, Ito, Sakamoto and Gray also have strong claims, which complicates the choice.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat early; the chemistry and cell biology are well reproduced.
uncertainties: Whether approvals will make the impact clearer in a few years.
Molecular glue and PROTAC contributions may need separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a transformative, general synthetic method used throughout pharmaceutical and materials chemistry, with clear mechanistic understanding of the catalytic cycle.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalysts independently; Kosugi reported the earlier tin-amide precursor. Credit is reasonably clear, but cross-coupling already received the 2010 prize, which affects how committees view the novelty.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of independent use. Timing is not a problem.
uncertainties: Whether Kosugi should be included or only the first two.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at free-electron lasers enables room-temperature structures of radiation-sensitive and non-crystallisable proteins and time-resolved structural movies of reactions, which combines spectroscopy with structure in the way I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Chapman for the principle and methods, Fromme for membrane-protein crystals and photosystem, Hajdu for the diffract-before-destroy concept. Schlichting is a notable alternative; credit is spread across method, concept and application.
assessment.maturity: Established, with growing but expensive, facility-limited confirmation; mechanistic discoveries from time-resolved work are still accumulating.
uncertainties: Relative importance of the method versus the science it produced.
Allocation among Chapman, Hajdu, Fromme and Schlichting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional and TROSY-type solution NMR methods made the structure and dynamics of large biomolecules accessible, giving atomic-level views of motion that bear on enzyme mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Bax and Clore for triple-resonance and structure methods, Kay for relaxation dispersion and methyl-TROSY of large complexes. Wüthrich's 2002 prize covers the foundations, and Wagner and Palmer have claims.
uncertainties: Method-driven candidacy with a diffuse contribution among many people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle in cells gives a physical-chemistry explanation for membraneless compartments, a concept with large conceptual reach.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne for the P-granule discovery, Rosen for the multivalent-interaction biophysics; Pappu and Mittag contributed the physical framework, so credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Interpretation is still debated, including physiological relevance and assay artefacts, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Biology versus chemistry framing, and credit among several leaders.
